title: Application for a stay of execution of sentence of death

pages.text:
No. ______________
_______________________________________
In the Supreme Court of the United States
_______________________________________
In re: Jamaal Howard,
Petitioner
_______________________________________
APPLICATION FOR STAY OF EXECUTION
_______________________________________
This is a capital case. Mr. Howard is scheduled to be executed
on Wednesday, October 7, 2026, after 6:00 p.m.
Petitioner Jamaal Howard is scheduled to be executed by the State of Texas after 
6:00 p.m. central time on Wednesday, October 7, 2026. He has filed in this Court a 
petition for a writ of mandamus asking the Court to direct the United States Court of 
Appeals for the Fifth Circuit to reconsider his motion for authorization to file a successive
habeas application without regard to the statute of limitations in 28 U.S.C. § 2244(d), a 
question Congress assigned to the district court. Howard asks the Court to stay his 
execution pending its consideration of that petition.
A stay is warranted when there is a fair prospect that a majority of the Court will 
grant the relief the applicant seeks and a likelihood that irreparable harm will result from 
the denial of a stay. Hollingsworth v. Perry, 558 U.S. 183, 190 (2010) (per curiam). Both 
conditions are met here. The petition presents a question that has divided the courts of 
appeals for nearly two decades: whether a court of appeals, ruling on a motion for 
authorization under § 2244(b)(3), may deny authorization on the ground that the

proposed application is untimely under § 2244(d). Pet. 1–2. Because § 2244(b)(3)(E) bars
certiorari review of authorization orders, that question can reach this Court only through 
an extraordinary writ. Pet. 7. And without a stay, Howard will be executed before the 
Court can consider his petition.
Howard respectfully asks the Court to stay his execution pending its consideration
of his petition for a writ of mandamus.
Respectfully submitted,
